definition: The product of a body's mass and its velocity, $p = mv$: a vector in the direction of the velocity, measured in kg m s⁻¹.
The average resultant force on a body multiplied by the time it acts, $J = F\Delta t$; it equals the body's change in momentum and the area under its force-time graph, measured in N s.
The rule that the total momentum of a system stays constant when no resultant external force acts on it; it holds in every collision and explosion of an isolated system.
In mechanics, a system on which no resultant external force acts, so its total momentum is constant; in thermal physics, a system that exchanges neither energy nor matter with its surroundings.
